argument.text: Let J=[r/2,3r/2] and take compact C from H003. M005 gives compact C×J. The continuous e_t is bounded there by K and vanishes outside C. The function b=K·1_C is integrable since C is compact and has finite Lebesgue measure. For F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and F′(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ), every F(τ) is strongly measurable by continuity, F(r) integrable by N001, and F′(r) strongly measurable. Smoothness gives the pointwise derivative in τ, and |F′(τ)(x)|≤b(x) for τ∈J. M006 therefore applies and gives E differentiable at r with derivative ∫e_t(x,r)dx. This proves N002 for arbitrary r.

hypothesis_checks: r lies in the open neighborhood interval.
Each F(τ) is continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
F′(r) is continuous and strongly measurable.
Compactness of C×J and continuity bound e_t on C; it vanishes outside C, yielding domination.
K1_C is integrable because C has finite Lebesgue measure.
Smoothness proves the pointwise derivative identity.
Both factors are Euclidean topological spaces.
J is a compact closed bounded interval.
